title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear portions and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, it's essential to consume enough iron and folate to ensure the health of both mother and baby. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports fetal development. In this article, we'll introduce three recipes rich in iron and folate that can be cooked in under 30 minutes.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Broccoli Bowl with Orange
* 100g grilled chicken (iron: 1.5mg)
* 100g steamed broccoli (iron: 2.5mg, vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 orange (vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 cup cooked white rice (folate: 10mcg)

Grilled chicken is an excellent source of heme iron, while broccoli and orange provide vitamin C to enhance iron absorption. To ensure food safety, choose fresh chicken and cook it thoroughly.

## Recipe 2: Pan-Seared Salmon and Green Beans Bowl with Lemon
* 100g pan-seared salmon (iron: 1.2mg)
* 100g steamed green beans (iron: 1.5mg, vitamin C: 100mg)
* 1 lemon (vitamin C: 70mg)
* 1 cup cooked white rice (folate: 10mcg)

Salmon is a rich source of heme iron and omega-3 fatty acids, while green beans and lemon provide vitamin C to enhance iron absorption. To ensure food safety, choose fresh salmon and cook it thoroughly.

## Recipe 3: Beef and Spinach Stir-Fry Bowl with Bell Peppers
* 100g beef stir-fry (iron: 2.5mg)
* 100g spinach stir-fry (iron: 2.5mg, vitamin C: 50mg)
* 1 bell pepper (vitamin C: 100mg)
* 1 cup cooked white rice (folate: 10mcg)

Beef stir-fry is an excellent source of heme iron, while spinach and bell peppers provide vitamin C to enhance iron absorption. To ensure food safety, choose fresh beef and cook it thoroughly.

## Food Safety Notes
During pregnancy, it's crucial to prioritize food safety. Avoid consuming:
* Raw or undercooked meat
* Raw or undercooked seafood
* Raw or undercooked eggs
* Soft cheeses that haven't been pasteurized

Visit our [website](/blog) for more information on pregnancy meal planning and food safety.

## Conclusion
These three recipes provide a rich source of iron and folate, supporting the health of both mother and baby. Remember to prioritize food safety and choose fresh, thoroughly cooked ingredients. For more information on prenatal nutrition, visit our [website](/blog/topics/prenatal-nutrition).

faqs.question: Why are iron and folate important for pregnant women?
faqs.answer: Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports fetal development.

faqs.question: How can I increase iron absorption?
faqs.answer: Consume vitamin C-rich foods like oranges, lemons, and bell peppers along with iron-rich foods.

faqs.question: Can I eat raw or undercooked foods during pregnancy?
faqs.answer: No, avoid consuming raw or undercooked foods to ensure food safety.
